[2] China denied the allegations. [3]

On the morning of November 12, Huang resigned as Nvidia's president and CEO. The company appointed its chief financial officer, [Colette Kress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colette_Kress), as interim CEO. [4] Huang will have no more formal roles at Nvidia, ending his 33 years at the company. [5]

## Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=1)]

Near the end of [Donald Trump's first presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_presidency_of_Donald_Trump), a growing number of Chinese companies became domiciled in Singapore, a practice termed "Singapore washing", which has since accelerated, spreading to various sectors from [critical minerals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critical_raw_materials) to tech and [biotechnology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biotechnology). With 28 [free trade agreements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade_agreement), Singapore was considered a good base to grow markets outside China. [6]

Megaspeed company logo

Megaspeed is a Singaporean [data center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center_services) firm. The company was incorporated in 2015 as 7Road International, owned by a Chinese investment holding company involved in the video game industry.[*[which?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Avoid_weasel_words)*] It grew substantially after President [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden) imposed restrictions on the sale of [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence) hardware to China in October 2022. 7Road International changed its name to Megaspeed International in March 2023. The Chinese split off the resulting company, [6] which was sold to Huang Le Limited. In October, 2023 Huang Le ended an eight-month tenure as managing director of Megaspeed, when the company was sold to a Singaporean company owned by Tan Yong Pong, who became Megaspeed's chief executive. [7] Four days after the sale, Megaspeed became an [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia) Cloud Partner. [8] By 2025, Megaspeed faced a U.S. probe for allegedly diverting Nvidia chips used for AI. [6]

## Alleged plot

*[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal)* reported that Jensen Huang was introduced to Alice Huang by Kang Wei, a Chinese businessman who Jensen knew for a decade; the Journal also reported that Kang and Alice Huang were married, and that Kang appeared to accept his wife's close relationship to Jensen Huang and spoke openly of their closeness. [9] In June 2024, Jensen Huang was seen with Alice Huang [a] (born 1982/1983 and of no relation to Jensen), a Chinese executive at Megaspeed. The two were seen together again in May 2025, and travelled in the same car. [10] [11] In October 2026, *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times)* published a piece alleging that Jensen had a close relationship with Alice, and that U.S. intelligence believed that Alice was a spy for China who relayed information about Jensen to the Chinese government. [2] On November 7, 2026, the *[Financial Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_Times)* reported that the [U.S. Intelligence Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Intelligence_Community) believed Alice Huang was recruited by the [Ministry of State Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_State_Security_(China)) (MSS). [12] The MSS has been described by diplomat [James Andrew Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Andrew_Lewis) as the largest and most active intelligence agency in the world, with an estimated 600,000 employees, and has largely focused on overseas Chinese nationals in its operations. [13] On November 8, 2026, Huang admitted to marital infidelity in a note addressed to "my colleagues at Nvidia". [14] Huang resigned as the CEO of Nvidia on November 12, 2026. [4] [15]

### Federal investigation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=4)]

As early as September 2024, the [United States Department of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Commerce)'s [Bureau of Industry and Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Industry_and_Security) had begun investigating Megaspeed and Alice Huang. [16] In August 2025, Tim Teter, Nvidia's general counsel, contacted officials at the bureau to request a meeting. Teter stated that he had received permission from [Jeffrey I. Kessler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_I._Kessler), the [under secretary of commerce for industry and security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_Commerce_for_Industry_and_Security), to discuss the case. The officials declined Teter's offer and forwarded the email to Kessler, who said that they should continue the inquiry lawfully. In an effort to prevent the investigation from being compromised, the inquiry was transferred to the [Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice), which opened a criminal investigation into Megaspeed. [17]

### Corporate investigation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=5)]

After *The New York Times* reported that Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, Nvidia opened an investigation into Jensen Huang. [18] [3] The board said on November 8 that it had no reason to believe national security or Nvidia secrets had been compromised. [19] The company hired New York-based law firm [Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wachtell,_Lipton,_Rosen_&_Katz) for the investigation. [20] On November 10, the independent directors said that former acting U.S. attorney [Joon H. Kim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joon_Kim) and the firm would conduct the investigation. [21]

## Responses

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=6)]

### Trump administration

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=7)]

Jensen Huang (right) and President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump) (left) in April 2025

According to *The New York Times*, President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump) had been briefed on the alleged spying in October 2025, but chose not to take action. [17] It also reported that Secretary of State [Marco Rubio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Rubio) had drafted a highly classified memo in spring 2026 warning of Huang's relationship, which was circulated to government officials with high-level security clearances before [Trump's visit to China in May 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_state_visit_by_Donald_Trump_to_China), which Huang joined. [22] Jensen Huang had a close relationship to Trump, which developed after Huang met the president at [Mar-a-Lago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mar-a-Lago) and donated to the [White House State Ballroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_State_Ballroom). Trump had previously refused to take actions that would disrupt Nvidia's sales—which had been bolstering the economy—or the United States's trade relationship with China. [2] At a Halloween party at Mar-a-Lago, Trump stated that he wanted Huang to remain on the [President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President's_Council_of_Advisors_on_Science_and_Technology), describing Huang as "very above board". [23]

President Trump introduces Jensen Huang and [Elon Musk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_Musk) to Chinese officials during a welcoming ceremony at [Beijing Capital International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beijing_Capital_International_Airport), 13 May 2026

On November 9, [CIA director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA_director) [John Ratcliffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Ratcliffe) and [Director of National Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_National_Intelligence) [Jay Clayton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Clayton) gave a closed-door briefing about Huang's affair to U.S. congressional leaders. [24] The same day, Trump stated that the [Federal Bureau of Investigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation) (FBI) was investigating Huang's affair. [25]

On November 12, U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Todd_Blanche) said "There’s no conclusions reached by the [Department of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice) or by me or by [FBI] Director [[Kash\] Patel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kash_Patel) around who she is or is not" and stated that Alice Huang being a spy is "something I have never said and that I don’t know to be true. So you assumed that DoJ learns that she is in fact a spy. Nobody said that. I certainly haven’t said that". [26]

### United States Congress

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=8)]

Florida representative [Brian Mast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Mast), the chair of the [House Committee on Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Foreign_Affairs); Michigan representative [John Moolenaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Moolenaar), the chair of the [House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Select_Committee_on_Strategic_Competition_between_the_United_States_and_the_Chinese_Communist_Party); and Arkansas representative [Rick Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Crawford_(politician)), the chair of the [House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Permanent_Select_Committee_on_Intelligence), requested that Huang appear before a closed-door briefing in November 2026. [27] On November 7, Delaware senator [Chris Coons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Coons), who is set to chair the [Senate Committee on Foreign Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Foreign_Relations), pledged to open an investigation on the 'insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires". [12]

### Jensen Huang

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=9)]

On November 8, Jensen Huang sent an apology to Nvidia employees admitting to marital infidelity. [14] Huang did not name who the other party in the affair was. [10]

On November 11, *The New York Times* reported that Huang had also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. The Associated Press said it could not independently confirm the report. [3]

On November 11, *The Wall Street Journal* reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to remove Huang as chief executive. [28] [29] On November 12, Nvidia announced that Huang had resigned as president, chief executive officer and a director, effective immediately. [Colette Kress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colette_Kress) was appointed interim chief executive while retaining her roles as executive vice president and chief financial officer. The board also appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first chair and began a search for a permanent chief executive. [4] [30] Following his resignation President Trump called on [Tim Cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Cook) to be chosen as Nvidia's new CEO. [26]

On November 12, [Reuters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reuters) reported that Huang had an 'intimate relationship' with a second female employee of Nvidia. [31]

### Nvidia investors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=10)]

The investigation occurred as concerns about the artificial intelligence industry mounted, contributing to Nvidia losing US$1.5 trillion in market capitalization within over a month. [32] That same day, investors filed a [class action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_action) lawsuit against Nvidia and Jensen Huang, accusing them of fraud for concealing Huang's ties with a suspected Chinese spy. [33]

### Megaspeed

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=11)]

On November 12, Megaspeed said it had cooperated with the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security and was prepared to cooperate with other U.S. government authorities. The company said it had hired a U.S. law firm to review its chip holdings and export controls. [3]

### Chinese government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=12)]

China's [Ministry of Foreign Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs_(China)) stated that *The New York Times* report was "pure fabrication out of thin air". [34] Chinese diplomat [Guo Jiakun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guo_Jiakun) called the report "smears against China". [25] Some Chinese [state media](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_media) reports have claimed that *The New York Times* report was aimed at destabilizing [U.S.–China relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China%E2%80%93United_States_relations). [25]

### Singapore government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jensen_Huang_spying_scandal&action=edit&section=13)]

In October 2025, [Singapore police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singapore_Police_Force) were investigating Megaspeed over "suspected breaches of our domestic laws". In October 2026, the [Ministry of Home Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Home_Affairs_(Singapore)) stated no investigations were conducted in ​respect of Alice ⁠Huang, while investigations into Megaspeed continued. Singapore said it did not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries", however it acts "firmly against companies and individuals who violate our laws and are engaged in fraudulent and dishonest practices". [7]

Jensen Huang, CEO of the chipmaking juggernaut Nvidia, is [stepping down](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-ceo-transition), the company's board announced Thursday.

The decision comes days after the company took the extraordinary step of [launching an investigation](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/statement-from-nvidia-board-of-directors) following news reports alleging that Huang had had an extramarital affair with one of the company's clients, who U.S. intelligence officials concluded had been recruited by China's top spy agency, [according to the *New York Times*](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/06/us/politics/chinese-spy-agency-nvidia-jensen-huang.html). NPR has not independently confirmed those reports.

### [News](https://www.npr.org/sections/news/)

### [Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's alleged relationship with Chinese spy](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/08/nx-s1-6034036/nvidia-launches-investigation-into-ceos-alleged-relationship-with-chinese-spy)

In [an email to Nvidia staff on Sunday,](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/a-message-to-our-company) Huang admitted to cheating on his wife, and said he would cooperate with the [investigation](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/08/nx-s1-6034036/nvidia-launches-investigation-into-ceos-alleged-relationship-with-chinese-spy).

The company's share price dropped sharply on Wednesday, after the *New York Times* [reported that Huang had had a second affair](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/technology/jensen-huang-nvidia-affair.html?searchResultPosition=2), this one with an Nvidia executive who reported to him.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to an NPR request for comment.

### [1A](https://www.npr.org/podcasts/510316/1a)

### [Tech: What The Nvidia Scandal Means For The Global Economy](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/11/nx-s1-6037485/tech-what-the-nvidia-scandal-means-for-the-global-economy)

Huang was widely seen as one of the most important business leaders in the United States. Nvidia dominates the market for the chips used to train and run artificial intelligence. Huang also had President Trump's ear on AI policy, with [Trump even calling Huang's phone](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-ai-speakerphone-all-hands-meeting-rcna597761) in September while Huang was onstage during a conference.

The scandal that brought down Huang snowballed quickly over the past two weeks. The *New York Times* [reported in late October](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html) that Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese woman at a Singapore-based company that was [buying Nvidia chips](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/10/09/technology/nvidia-chips-china-megaspeed.html). Citing unidentified sources, it said U.S. intelligence officials believed she had been recruited by the Chinese government to spy on him and possibly try to influence policy. NPR has not independently confirmed this reporting.

### [Here & Now Anytime](https://www.npr.org/podcasts/510051/here-x26-now)

### [The spy scandal rocking Nvidia](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/09/nx-s1-6034607/the-spy-scandal-rocking-nvidia)

A drip-drip of scoops followed — from the *Times* and other outlets — suggesting that [the relationship was romantic](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/technology/alice-huang-megaspeed-nvidia-jensen-huang.html), that senior Trump administration officials [knew about the allegations](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/us/politics/trump-china-trip-nvidia.html) some time ago, and that Huang had [had a second affair](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/11/technology/jensen-huang-nvidia-affair.html).

China's foreign ministry has said the allegations of spying are baseless and part of a smear campaign against China.

### What's next for Nvidia

Huang's departure launches Nvidia into uncharted territory.

Huang's relationship with the alleged Chinese agent and what the Trump administration knew about it will likely be the subject of an investigation when Democrats take control of Congress in January.

"We should all be extremely concerned about this, and the fact that the White House knew about this for weeks, maybe months now, is is is very disturbing as well," said Rep. Yvette Clarke, D-NY, a senior member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee in an interview with NPR.

The company's Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, has been appointed interim CEO. The board said in their statement they would conduct a full search for a new CEO and consider both internal and external candidates.

"There's no obvious replacement," said Stephen Witt, author of a book about Nvidia called *The Thinking Machine*. "It's not even clear Nvidia can be the same kind of company without Jensen. I have a hard time imagining what Nvidia looks like without Jensen."

Nvidia still plans to report its quarterly earnings on Tuesday.

Huang was one of the longest-serving CEOs in U.S. corporate history, stepping into the role after launching the company with partners over bottomless cups of [coffee at a Denny's](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-dennys-trillion/) restaurant in San Jose, Calif., 33 years ago. Nvidia got its start making specialized chips to create 3D graphics for computers that would come to be known as graphics processing units, or GPUs.

He was the face of Nvidia and an unlikely celebrity, giving countless [keynote](https://www.nvidia.com/gtc/keynote/) speeches and [interviews](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lZ74RhUsrMs) in his trademark leather jacket, or posing for [selfies](https://www.wsj.com/world/asia/jensen-huang-nvidia-ceo-taiwan-fame-99630726) with adoring fans.

Huang was also the company's driving force. Under his leadership, Nvidia made a big and early bet on artificial intelligence, investing heavily to transform its niche graphics chips into general-purpose processing units that were ideal for the volume of computations required to create AI.

### [Machine Gods](https://www.npr.org/podcasts/g-s1-143588/machine-gods)

### [What now for Nvidia's Jensen Huang, and should Congress ban RSI?](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/11/nx-s1-6036816/what-now-for-nvidias-jensen-huang-and-should-congress-ban-rsi)

That bet would pay off in spades as GPUs became the go-to chip for AI creators. When AI burst into the public consciousness in late 2022 with the launch of OpenAI's ChatGPT — a chatbot trained and run on Nvidia chips — the firm was worth about $400 billion. Today, it's valued at more than $4 trillion, among the most valuable in the world, and it dominates the market for GPUs.

But analysts say despite Huang's visionary management of the business, he had a blind spot for succession and hadn't articulated a clear plan, at least publicly.

In a Bloomberg [interview](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2026-11-09/jensen-huang-on-who-could-succeed-him-as-nvidia-ceo-video) from mid-October, Huang was vague about succession plans. "I'm really hoping that the next CEO of the company is already at the company, but 20 years from now, I hope I stay healthy and I hope I continue to earn my keep."

Huang's adult children, Spencer and Madison Huang, [both work at Nvidia](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/what-to-know-about-nvidias-investigation-after-ceos-affair-98df3bba). Asked about talk that Madison might be in line to succeed him, he paused, and told Bloomberg: "if that's their aspiration, Spencer or Madison's, they have to go earn it. And it's really, really hard work. It takes a lot of sacrifice."

Daniel Newman, CEO of the Futurum Group, a tech research firm, said the company will inevitably be different without Huang, and its future success is unclear.

"They've always had Jensen as this sort of visionary at the front," he said. "I don't think that's replaceable."

# Timeline of a scandal: How Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation unfolded at Nvidia - CBS News
URL: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jensen-huang-nvidia-resignation-scandal-timeline/
Type: text/html

Jensen Huang's [departure from Nvidia](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns/) caps a tumultuous week for the chipmaker, with his resignation coming less than a week after his extramarital [relationship](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-jensen-huang-investigation-china-intelligence/) with a suspected Chinese spy became public.

But the seeds for Huang's downfall were planted much earlier. The woman with whom he had a relationship, Alice Huang (no relation), arrived on the tech scene in 2023, when she became the managing director of Singapore-based data center [Megaspeed International](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/megaspeed-nvidia-china-ties/).

Megaspeed, which on Thursday said it has complied with U.S. laws, would proceed to buy billions of dollars in Nvidia chips and servers. Over the past two years, Alice Huang, also known by her Chinese name Huang Le, has been photographed and recorded socializing with Jensen Huang, prompting questions in May from one quizzical investor about their "uncomfortably close relationship."

Below is a timeline of events that led to Huang's startling resignation on Thursday.

## November 2015

Alice Huang, a former television reporter in China, joins investment firm Shanghai Hexi Investment Management as deputy general manager, according to social media posts and records from Simuwang, a Chinese private equity database. Shanghai Hexi was founded by Kang Wei, who became her husband, [according](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/a-mystery-businessman-introduced-jensen-huang-to-his-paramourher-husband-1ec3b581) to the Wall Street Journal.

## March 2023

7Road International, originally incorporated in Singapore in 2015 as 7Road International, is renamed Megaspeed, and ownership of the "neocloud" company is transferred to Huang Le Ltd., an enterprise controlled by Alice Huang. She becomes its managing director.

## June 2023

Cloud-computing company Shanghai Century Litong is founded. A company linked to Alice's sister, Huang Yu, held an ownership stake.

## October 2023

Nvidia designates Shanghai Century Litong as a preferred cloud partner, giving the Chinese company priority access to Nvidia's chips, according to [The Information](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/jensen-huangs-yearslong-ties-alice-huang-enabled-nvidia-chip-sales-china).

## Around November 2023

Megaspeed's shares were transferred to another Singapore company, Swiftdata, and Alice Huang ceased to be listed as a director of the company, according to news site Caixin Global.

## June 7, 2024

Information technology firm NetThunder posted a picture on social media of Alice Huang and Jensen Huang with other tech executives at a bar in Taipei, Taiwan.

## End of 2024

Megaspeed's assets exploded from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024, according to financial filings [reviewed](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/what-we-know-about-megaspeed-singapore-based-customer-nvidia-2026-11-10/) by Reuters.

Shipment records from December 2024 through early 2026, [analyzed](https://culperresearch.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Culper_NVDA_5-13-2026.pdf) by short-selling firm Culper Research, suggest that Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary, Speedmatrix, imported about $4 billion in products from a company that builds equipment with Nvidia chips.

## Early 2025

Alice Huang and her husband, Kang Wei, jointly pitched Chinese investors on a Southeast Asia data center project, reportedly telling them they had "no problem securing GPUs" — the graphics processing units Nvidia specializes in — and citing Alibaba as a customer, [according](https://www.ft.com/content/5d8c1e1d-6ce0-4eb4-9f5c-722fa5c4841d?syn-25a6b1a6=1) to the Financial Times.

## January 31, 2025

Jensen Huang meets with President Trump at the White House. It marks their first of many White House encounters in Mr. Trump's second term.

## February 2025

Singapore [opens](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-12/singapore-says-warns-alice-huang-lacks-evidence-of-offenses)an investigation into Megaspeed and several other companies over suspected false declarations related to the purchase of servers and other offenses, according to Bloomberg News.

## May 22, 2025

Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are recorded on video together at a dinner at San Liu Shi Fu restaurant in Taipei, around the time of the Computex tech conference in Taiwan.

## July 2025

Jensen Huang says the technology giant has [won approval](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-says-it-has-trump-administration-green-light-to-sell-its-advanced-h20-computer-chips-used-for-ai-to-china/)from the Trump administration to sell its advanced H20 computer chips, used to develop artificial intelligence, to China, a reversal of prior administration policy.

"It's so innovative and dynamic here in China that it's really important that American companies are able to compete and serve the market here in China," Huang said at the time.

That same month, Nvidia becomes the first public company to be worth $4 trillion.

## February 2026

Chinese police detained Kang Wei, Alice Huang's husband and business partner, in connection with suspected stock manipulation, sources told Caixin.

That same month, Singapore barred Alice Huang from re-entering the country after she downplayed her role at Megaspeed amid the country's investigation into its operations, according to a Bloomberg News [report.](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-12/singapore-says-warns-alice-huang-lacks-evidence-of-offenses)

## May 12, 2026

Jensen Huang boards Air Force One in Alaska to accompany Mr. Trump on a two-day trip to Beijing.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio briefed Mr. Trump about the counterintelligence risk posed by Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang, [according](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/us/politics/rubio-nvidia-ceo-chinese-spy.html) to the New York Times. The briefing, which occurred before Jensen Huang joined the trip, was the second briefing Mr. Trump had received from U.S. intelligence about the Nvidia CEO's relationship, the Times reported.

## September 24, 2026

Jensen Huang attends Mr. Trump's state dinner for China's Xi Jinping at the White House.

## September 29, 2026

Jensen Huang attends an AI event at the White House and signs a set of voluntary AI [safety standards](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-ai-constitution-tech-execs-openai-anthropic-voluntary-controls/) amid calls for tighter guardrails on the technology.

## November 8, 2026

Jensen Huang writes a message to Nvidia employees admitting that he had an extramarital affair. The same day, Nvidia's board [said](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/statement-from-nvidia-board-of-directors) it had launched an independent investigation amid reports that its CEO was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort."

The New York Times on Nov. 8 [reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/technology/nvidia-investigation-jensen-huang-china.html) that U.S. government surveillance suggested Alice Huang was feeding information directly to Beijing.

## November 9, 2026

At an impromptu press conference at the White House, Mr. Trump said he had spoken to Jensen Huang and that the tech exec had indicated he was unaware of Alice Huang's links to China's intelligence services. Mr. Trump also described the Nvidia CEO as an "honorable man" who's "definitely suffering."

## November 12, 2026

Nvidia's board of directors [announces](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns/) that Jensen Huang has resigned, effective immediately.

In June 2013, President Barack Obama welcomed Chinese President [Xi Jinping](https://www.cnbc.com/xi-jinping/) to Sunnylands, a secluded California estate, for an informal summit. Behind the diplomatic pleasantries, Obama confronted Xi over Chinese state-directed cyber-enabled espionage and theft of American intellectual property, warning that such activities threatened American companies and the broader bilateral relationship.

Thirteen years after the Sunnylands Summit, the threat has evolved significantly as the race to dominate [AI](https://www.cnbc.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/) frames the U.S.-China relationship. The stakes are higher, the technology more consequential, and the vulnerabilities increasingly involve attempts to compromise or coopt the "key man" at the helm of the nation's top technology companies.

With the unfolding scandal involving [Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/jensen-huang-nvidia-china-ties.html), the blame should start with the CEO himself, but it should not end there. The situation illustrates a failure of Silicon Valley, corporate and political leadership at a much wider level.

Huang has [acknowledged an extramarital affair](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/nvidia-jensen-huang-email-board-of-directors-statement.html) with a woman identified in reporting as Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based [Megaspeed](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/megaspeed-nvidia-jensen-huang-alice-huang.html), an Nvidia customer. American intelligence officials [reportedly believe](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html) she was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information and potentially influence Nvidia's efforts to loosen American semiconductor export restrictions. China denies the allegations.

Nvidia's independent directors have [launched an investigation](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/nvidia-jensen-huang-investigation.html), and so far, they say no compromise of company secrets or national security information has been established. But the problem extends well beyond Huang or Nvidia. Focusing exclusively on whether proprietary technology or trade secrets were transferred fundamentally misunderstands the potential intelligence value of such an operation.

For Beijing, gaining insight into, influencing, or potentially compromising American technology policymaking could be equally valuable. Advance knowledge of export-control deliberations, regulatory intentions, negotiating positions, or divisions within the administration could provide strategic advantages without a single semiconductor design being stolen.

The Trump administration reportedly received warnings about the relationship before the scandal became public. Nevertheless, Huang remained an influential participant in semiconductor policy discussions while advocating greater access to China's market.

[New reporting](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/09/business/economy/nvidia-megaspeed-investigation-huang.html) also raises questions about interactions between Nvidia and Commerce Department officials during an investigation into Megaspeed, subsequently transferred to the Justice Department. No improper influence has been established, but corporate access to government decision-making deserves scrutiny alongside proprietary technology.

### It is a new era of 'key man' risk with AI

Whether appropriate protective measures were taken remains unclear. President [Donald Trump's public defense of Huang](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/09/trump-jensen-huang-nvidia-chinese-spy.html) — saying that Huang told him he had no idea the woman could be a spy and that he trusted the CEO, and that if national intelligence had warned the president about this threat, as has been reported, he didn't remember — hardly conveyed the urgency warranted by allegations of a foreign intelligence operation targeting a strategically indispensable American company.

Trump has met Xi three times since returning to office, with two additional encounters anticipated in November and December. These meetings offer Trump an opportunity to follow Obama's example by confronting Xi directly over Chinese state-directed or sponsored espionage targeting American technology companies, their executives, and potentially the U.S. policymaking process.
